description: De Staat der Nederlanden nodigt u als potentiële inschrijver uit om in te schrijven voor de openbare Europese aanbesteding voor de aanschaf van een SAAS-oplossing inzake constructiesoftware voor het kunnen maken en beheren van examenvragen voor de Wet Financieel Toezicht (hierna: Wft). Doel is het afsluiten van een dienstverleningsovereenkomst met één leverancier. Het doel van de Opdracht is het verwerven van constructiesoftware welke gebruikt kan worden om Wft-examens te maken die naar Facet geëxporteerd kunnen worden. Deze examens maken deel uit van het vakbekwaamheidsstelsel Wft. Deze aanbesteding is van toepassing voor het constructiedeel, dus voor enkel de software om de examenvragen te maken en te beheren. Wij zoeken een SAAS-oplossing met het doel: Het faciliteren van DUO om het niveau van zijn huidige dienstverlening, op het gebied van de constructie van examens en de ontvangst door Facet van items (met metadata) voor deze examens te behouden en/of verhogen. De geraamde omvang van de opdracht is door DUO vastgelegd in het inkoopstartformulier en is aangevuld met informatie vanuit de marktconsultatie. De totale geschatte opdrachtwaarde voor 10 jaar (incl. eventuele verlengingen) bedraagt € 2.350.000 excl. btw. Let op: de gegevens die de omvang van de opdracht aangeven zijn een indicatie op basis vanuit het verleden en voor de komende jaren. Aan deze omvang kunnen geen rechten aan worden ontleend.

description: The Council seeks to identify an Economic Operator to act as a Development Partner to work in collaboration with the Council, to identify the optimal solution for Council owned lands within the adopted Clonburris SDZ located at Kishoge Urban Centre (SDCC Site 06), subsectors KUC-S1, KUC-S2 and KUC-S3 in compliance with the adopted SDZ and the Council’s requirements. The Council’s vision is to deliver a sustainable, high quality neighbourhood for Kishogue Urban Centre as Phase 6 of the Clonburris Development. These social, affordable and cost rental homes will be delivered in accordance with the following supporting national and local policies; Clonburris Strategic Development Zone Planning Scheme, South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2022-2028, Housing For All; A new Housing Plan for Ireland 2030, Housing delivery Action Plan 2022-2026 The development site has an estimated capacity for approximately 640 units (subject to planning permission). The required tenure mix is anticipated to be 120 social housing units to be sold to the Council, a minimum of 260 affordable purchase dwellings to be sold to eligible persons under the Scheme of Priority for Affordable Dwellings and a maximum of 260 cost rental units. The tenure types are to be split by block. Delivery of 900m2 of commercial property split over 3 selected ground floor locations across KUC-S1, KUC-S2 and KUC-S3 to facilitate employment or retail use within the wider development. Progress site identification for 6300 m2 of employment use for future development. A location for the employment use has been identified on the included schematic, this does not have to be the final location. The Council is seeking to identify an economic operator that has the requisite skillset and is considered most capable of working in collaboration with the Council, to identify the optimal solution for the development site in accordance with the SDZ and the Council’s requirement and to deliver it as efficiently as possible.

title: France – Installation of telecommunications equipment – ACBC - RVT – TELECOM – Partie Télécom (multi territoire) - 6 lots
description: Accord-cadre multi-attributaire à bons de commande, passé sans engagement de commande et sans montant minimum, avec un montant maximum par lot, portant sur des travaux de télécommunications ferroviaires. Il est décomposé en 6 lots géographiques : Lot PACA, Lot LANGUEDOC ROUSSILLON, Lot RHONE, Lot ALPES, Lot AUVERGNE NIVERNAIS et Lot BOURGOGNE FRANCHE COMPTE. Les travaux comprennent notamment : l’aménagement de locaux télécoms (baies, coffrets, têtes de câbles optiques, chemins de câbles, mise à la terre) ; l’aménagement des prises et tableaux de distribution d’énergie ; le déroulage, le raccordement et les tests de câbles courants faibles (cuivre, LAN, fibre optique) ; le déroulage et le raccordement de câbles courants forts alimentant les installations télécoms ; la pose d’équipements télécoms en gare et sur quai (écrans de téléaffichage, caméras, haut-parleurs, balises sonores, horloges, bornes wifi, antennes, supports et mâts) ; la pose de fourreaux et tubes PEHD, de câbles cuivre et de fibres optiques ; la confection de prises de terre et de terres longitudinales ; les travaux de petit génie civil associés (massifs, fourreaux, percements, bris de béton). Les détails sont précisés au DCE. Chaque lot est attribué à deux titulaires : le titulaire de rang 1 (mieux-disant) et le titulaire de rang 2 (second mieux-disant). Les bons de commande sont répartis en montant à hauteur de 70 % (± 10 %) pour le titulaire de rang 1 et de 30 % (± 10 %) pour le titulaire de rang 2, sur chaque période d’exécution. Cette répartition s’applique aux bons de commande effectivement émis et ne constitue pas un engagement de volume. Le montant de chaque bon de commande est plafonné à 200 000 € HT. L’accord-cadre comprend une tranche ferme de 2 ans, du 10/05/2027 au 09/05/2029, et une reconduction éventuelle d’un an, du 10/05/2029 au 09/05/2030. Les candidats peuvent candidater à un ou plusieurs lots. Un même soumissionnaire ne peut être attributaire de plus de 2 lots en rang 1 et de plus de 2 lots en rang 2, selon les règles précisées dans le règlement de consultation.

title: Norway – Works for complete or part construction and civil engineering work – Loppa municipality - Molo - Øksfjord Harbour
description: On behalf of Loppa municipality, tenderers are invited to a competition for improvements to the port conditions in Øksfjord. The General contract (NS 8406) includes the establishment of two new piers, the establishment of a new pumping station, a sewage pipeline and an access road. Dredging the seabed under Molo South is necessary to ensure sufficient geotechnical stability before completion. Dredging masses shall be reused as core masses in the piers and for filling ditches, while any surplus matter is delivered to an approved site. The work shall be carried out with environmental measures such as bubble curtain and turbidity monitoring. The existing sewage pipeline must have been moved and relaid with a new pumping station before sea work starts. The pier North shall be partially established before dredging starts to enable encapsulation of the dredging masses and reduce particle dispersion. The contract includes further filling work, width expansion and extension of Pier North, establishment of a turnaround, as well as concrete work on a new and existing pier. The concrete works are options and include casting breakwater covers, parapets and casting on existing constructions. The builder is free to order all or parts of the optioned concrete works. The execution shall be carried out in accordance with the engineering design documentation and the accompanying drawings. Furthermore, there are option posts for the demolition and re-establishment of approx. 200 metres of existing sewage pipeline on land.

title: Data & AI Mission Expert Services (DAMES) IDIQ
description: The Department of the Air Force Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Officer (DAF CDAO in SAF/CND) is conducting market intelligence to identify sources for a potential requirement for Data & AI Mission Expert Services (DAMES) IDIQ support services in accordance with the attached Performance Work Statement. The Government is still in the early acquisition planning stage and all activities at this time are considered market intelligence. This is a Request for Information (RFI) and is NOT a request for proposals and the information received will be utilized for acquisition planning purposes. Responders are advised that the Government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred with response to this announcement and information submitted in response to this RFI will not be returned. 1.0 REQUESTED INFORMATION 1.1 Capability Statement: Request you submit a capability statement that presents your technical capability for completing the attached Performance Work Statement. The capability statement shall at a minimum address the specific items below. 1.1.1 Approach: Describe your approach for accomplishing the Performance Work Statement. 1.1.2 Past Performance: Identify previous contracts which are relevant to the scope of the Performance Work Statement. Include contract number, period of performance, whether performance was completed as a prime or subcontract, and a summary of services provided. 1.1.3 Timeline: Attached your timeline in obtaining the required skill set for contract award. This timeline should include time for any applicable transition period, clearances (if required), and any other information that would be crucial to successfully transition to contract award. 1.1.4 Page Limit: Capability Statements are limited to 15 pages in total length, single spaced, and 12-point font and accessible by either Microsoft Word or Adobe Acrobat. 1.2 Submission Instructions: Please provide your responses to this RFI to the primary POC listed in this announcement by the timeframe listed in this announcement. Additionally, please include your company's CAGE, Unique Entity ID, and Size Standard as part of your submission. Please note: Large submissions may be required to be sent via multiple e-mails. The Government recommends contacting the primary POC in this announcement to verify receipt. 1.3 Industry Discussions: The Government may choose to meet with companies who responded to this RFI to hold one-on-one discussions. Discussions would only be held to obtain further clarification of potential capability to meet the requirement. 1.4 Proposed Acquisition Strategy: The Government is contemplating using the Highest Technically Rated Offeror (HRTO) selection methodology for this acquisition. This allows the Government to promote efficiency in acquisition through a streamlined selection decision, especially for this knowledge based services where technical ability is of paramount concern. The Government would like to solicit industry feedback for this acquisition approach regarding the pros/cons that industry perceives with the acquisition approach. 1.5 Industry Feedback Regarding Requirement: While the Government is the final decision regarding the requirement, we would like to solicit industry feedback regarding the attached requirements documentation and where industry thinks that we could improve the overall quality of the product/service received by updating/clarifying our requirement.

description: U.S. ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY Request for Information (RFI) Regarding the Next Generation of EPA�s Superfund Remediation Acquisition Framework (RAF) Contracts Attachment, "RFI - Body" includes identical information as found below, however may be more easily read from a formatting standpoint. Request for Information (RFI) The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is posting these draft requirements (see attachments) and questions to obtain feedback from industry to help shape the next generation of contracts supporting the Superfund Remedial Program. EPA�s goal is to increase the performance-based aspects of the requirements, providing more flexibility to contractors in how work is performed while ensuring EPA receives the necessary services/deliverables. Contractors are welcome to make Track Changes within the attached draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) and resubmit recommendations back to the agency for consideration. Additionally, EPA has included a list of questions below on specific topics for feedback. It is the Government�s intent to use the recommendations and feedback received from industry to help better inform the strategic direction of the procurement process (e.g. requirement refinement, improvement, or clarification), but is under no obligation to incorporate any proposed changes into the final PWS. All information and documentation posted under this notice is preliminary in nature and may be updated or amended prior to the release of the formal solicitation. The agency intends to post draft solicitations for each requirement at a later date for industry questions and/or feedback. Additionally, EPA is developing an external-facing website to enable future posting of information and facilitate communication. It is EPA�s hope the website will be used not only to facilitate communication between EPA and industry regarding the next generation of contracts, but also be a useful resource for intra-industry communication for Prime/Sub relationship building. A future notification will be posted when the external website is operational. This notice does not constitute a formal solicitation. Once a solicitation is posted, all responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered by the agency. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay any cost incurred in response to this notice; all costs associated with responding to this notice will solely be at the interested parties� expense. Any information provided by industry to the Government as a result of this notice is voluntary. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future solicitation(s). The questions in this RFI are for market research and information-gathering purposes only. They do not reflect final agency requirements, preferences, or decisions, and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Agency to any particular acquisition strategy, scope, contract type, or solicitation content. Basic information on the current Remedial Acquisition Framework (RAF) program and contracts is located at https://www.epa.gov/superfund/remedial-acquisition-framework. EPA will not post any of the responses received for these questions. Only submissions made via FedConnect by the closing date/time are permitted. NO EMAILS. NO PHONE CALLS. NO OTHER SUBMISSION METHODS AUTHORIZED. The Agency may use Super Intelligence (SI) tools to analyze or summarize industry responses; however, Government personnel will review all submissions and make all decisions. The Agency is seeking industry input on these topics only at this time; additional opportunities to ask questions will be provided later in the acquisition process. QUESTIONS FOR INDUSTRY: Topic 1: Geographic Structure & Competition EPA is considering awarding multiple award contracts based upon four (4) geographic zones (Regions 1�3; 4+6; 5+7; 8�10) based on regional profiles and programmatic needs. Vendor pools may be limited per suite and per zone to ensure meaningful participation and reduce task order award cycle time. 1. What assumptions should EPA provide to enable accurate pricing on early stage tasks? Topic 3: Discrete Investigation and Site Cleanup Operations (DISCO) Suite The Agency is considering the addition of another suite of acquisition vehicles, DISCO, to provide rapid response services to support urgent, discrete, and short-term field needs (e.g., single sampling events, installing security fencing, etc.) with the goal of awarding competitively placed task orders within 30-calendar days. description:
L’Université Bastion à Genève fait l’objet d’un projet global de rénovation visant une transformation à la fois architecturale et fonctionnelle de l’ensemble existant. L’objectif des travaux est une revalorisation durable de la structure bâtie, en tenant compte des exigences actuelles en matière d’architecture, d’usage, de technique et d’efficacité énergétique.


L’accent est mis sur le développement respectueux du patrimoine bâti historique, tout en intégrant des standards contemporains sur le plan des infrastructures et de l’expression architecturale. Dans ce contexte, des aspects tels que la qualité des espaces, la flexibilité des usages ainsi qu’une approche architecturale claire jouent un rôle central.


Les travaux ont d’ores et déjà débuté et l’exploitation du site se poursuit actuellement dans un contexte de chantier en cours. La mise en service est prévue pour l’année académique 2027 / 2028.


Cet appel d'offre se déroulera en deux phases. Au premier tour, les soumissionnaires devront fournir les documents demandés ainsi que les échantillons de la lentille et du support en métal, selon les indications de l'appel d'offres. description: L’Université Bastion à Genève fait l’objet d’un projet global de rénovation visant une transformation à la fois architecturale et fonctionnelle de l’ensemble existant. L’objectif des travaux est une revalorisation durable de la structure bâtie, en tenant compte des exigences actuelles en matière d’architecture, d’usage, de technique et d’efficacité énergétique. L’accent est mis sur le développement respectueux du patrimoine bâti historique, tout en intégrant des standards contemporains sur le plan des infrastructures et de l’expression architecturale. Dans ce contexte, des aspects tels que la qualité des espaces, la flexibilité des usages ainsi qu’une approche architecturale claire jouent un rôle central. Les travaux ont d’ores et déjà débuté et l’exploitation du site se poursuit actuellement dans un contexte de chantier en cours. La mise en service est prévue pour l’année académique 2027 / 2028. Cet appel d'offre se déroulera en deux phases. Au premier tour, les soumissionnaires devront fournir les documents demandés ainsi que les échantillons de la lentille et du support en métal, selon les indications de l'appel d'offres. Après analyse des dossiers transmis, 3 candidats seront sélectionnés et invités à participer à la 2e phase en fonction des critères de sélection.

description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT (NPP) Solicitation No. W4938-26F14 Requirement: 74height-adjustable extended-corner workstations. Client: Department of National Defence Destination: 60Moodie Drive, Carling Campus, Ottawa, Ontario, Building 9, Level 1 and 2 South Required by 31 March 2027 1. This Notice of Proposed Procurement is issued pursuant to the mandatory Public Works and Government Services Canada Office Furniture for Workspaces Supply Arrangement E60PQ-140003/D and covers Product Category 2 - Work Surface Products. 2. The Department of National Defence (the “Client”) requires the purchase, delivery and installation of 74 complete electric height-adjustable extended-corner workstations at 60 Moodie Drive, Carling Campus, Ottawa, Ontario, Building 9, Level 1 South. Delivery and installation must be completed no later than 31 March 2027. 3. . The work includes all hardware, materials, labour, supervision, tools and equipment required for delivery to the final locations, assembly, levelling, testing, protection of the premises, cleanup and warranty documentation. The workstations are nominally 70 in. x 70 in., with nominal 23 in. depth on both sections. Suppliers must refer to the attached solicitation documents, including the draft solicitation and its annexes, for the complete statement of requirements, mandatory technical criteria, specifications, deliverables, evaluation requirements, and draft terms and conditions. 4. This requirement will be solicited among suppliers holding a valid supply arrangement under the General Supplier Stream for Product Category 2 - Work Surface Products. Only suppliers qualified under the applicable category and stream are eligible to submit a bid. Equivalent products may be proposed where they meet every mandatory technical requirement and are supported by the required evidence. 5. The Indigenous procurement assessment has been completed. This requirement is not set aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business and will proceed through the General Supplier Stream. The following trade agreements apply to this procurement: the Canadian Free Trade Agreement, the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement, the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, the Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement, the Canada-Ukraine Free Trade Agreement, and Canada's applicable bilateral free trade agreements. 6. Security and site-access requirements are not fully evidenced in the current file. The approved security determination, including whether an SRCL or specific personnel/site-access controls are required, must be confirmed and the appropriate wording inserted before publication. 7. The basis of selection is the responsive offer with the highest combined price and delivery score, subject to the final solicitation terms. The evaluation allocates 70 points to evaluated price and 30 points to the proposed period for completing delivery and installation. 8. Funding approval and commitment, the solicitation issue date, enquiry deadline, closing date and time, authorised submission channel, and current mandatory Supply Arrangement and departmental clauses were completed and approved before issue. title: Ireland – Building and facilities management services – M700.CN.1025 - Soft Facilities Management Services for MetroLink (TII)
description: Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII), acting as the Sponsoring Agency for the Dublin MetroLink programme, is seeking to appoint a contractor for the provision of Soft Facilities Management (Soft FM) Services for MetroLink. TII has signed a new 10-year lease, with the option to extend up to a maximum of 15 years, for the MetroLink project team at Coopers Cross, a landmark mixed-use campus in Dublin’s North Docklands. The services to be included in the scope of this contract will be: • Staff requirements for the Coopers Cross Office including 2 x reception staff and 2 x facilities assistants. • Cleaning services and consumables; • Coffee machines (rental, servicing, maintenance, beans etc); • Office stationery and supplies; • Courier services; • Taxi services; • Postal services; • Franking machine services; • Canteen supplies (tea, coffee, sugar, biscuits); • Confidential shredding services; • Facilities equipment maintenance; • Fire extinguisher and first aid equipment maintenance (MetroLink controlled areas only); • Smoke detector servicing (MetroLink controlled areas only); • Zip Tap maintenance and Co2 supply (Coopers Cross office); and • Further Soft FM services to cater for support for MetroLink site offices to be set up in future.

title: Supply of Army Branded Clothing
description: Unite Procurement UK Limited (part of Unite Holding SE), on behalf of the Ministry of Defence, is seeking suppliers to join the Unite Procurement Platform. The authority requires the supply of a standardised package of Army-branded clothing. Providing practical, recognisable and consistent clothing for public-facing recruitment and engagement events, routine travel and outdoor activity. A consistent clothing package is required to improve professional presentation, support Army branding and provide practical clothing suitable for the environments in which the teams operate. Provide a consistent and professional Army identity across Arms & Services Engagement Teams. Provide practical clothing suitable for travel, public events and outdoor engagement activity. Deliver a one-off issue that requires no ongoing maintenance, repair or replacement commitment from the Authority. Included: manufacture, Army branding, packaging and delivery of complete clothing packages in the sizes confirmed by the Authority. Included: one coordinated delivery, unless an alternative delivery schedule is agreed in writing by the Authority. Excluded: recurring supply, replacement for loss or damage, repair, laundering, alteration after acceptance, and ongoing stock management. Requirements The Contractor shall provide complete clothing packages. Each package shall contain: One quilted puffer jacket. One softshell jacket. One pair of stretch trousers. Three moisture-wicking T-shirts. Three pairs of physical training shorts. The Unite Procurement Platform (Unite | Simplify indirect procurement with our smarter platform) offers a compliant route to market for UK Public Sector organisations to manage low-value, high-volume procurement. How to Apply Interested suppliers should register their interest by contacting Unite Procurement UK Limited and provide details of their product range, modification capabilities, and maintenance services. Further information on the onboarding process for the Unite Procurement Platform will be provided upon expression of interest and can also be found at the link attached. Unite Procurement UK Limited does not intend to appoint a sole supplier for this requirement. Instead, multiple suppliers may be onboarded to the Unite Procurement Platform to ensure a diverse and competitive supply base, supporting flexibility and choice for the Ministry of Defence and associated organisations. Suppliers are encouraged to express their interest by the stated closing date to ensure early consideration. However, applications to join the Unite Procurement Platform will be welcome at any time beyond the initial deadline. Unite Procurement UK Limited reserves the right to review and onboard new suppliers on a rolling basis to meet evolving requirements and to maintain a dynamic and responsive supplier network. For any enquiries and interest, please email defence.support@unite.eu with the subject title "TSS 809 Opportunity"

title: Debris Boom Supply and Install at Harry S. Truman Lake Project
description: The solicitation is amended to provide revisions to the Purchase Description, CLIN Structure, provide a Projnet Plan Room key to access the Bathymetry survey information and extend the quote due date. Also, Contractor Questions Answered Part 2 are posted. Contractor Questions/Government Answers are posted. The purpose of the debris boom is to prevent floating debris from impacting the dam's tainter gates, which is crucial for maintaining the full operational capacity of the spillway. The boom will also serve as a visual barrier to boaters. The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, engineering, fabrication, delivery, and optional installation necessary to furnish a complete debris boom system at Harry S. Truman Dam. The approximately 2,000-foot boom shall be designed to intercept floating debris upstream of the spillway and withstand site-specific hydraulic, wind, wave, debris, and impact loading conditions. The debris boom shall be designed for an 800-foot-long by 3-foot-thick debris field, use a minimum safety factor of 2.0 for design loads, withstand a direct head-on impact from an 18-inch-diameter, 100-foot-long log traveling at the maximum design water velocity, and withstand design conditions including 50 mph wind speed and 5-foot wave height. This acquisition is not set-aside for small business concerns and is competed as full and open competition, Unrestricted. An organized site visit has been scheduled for: Friday, 9 October 2026 at 11am.

title: C1DA-- AE Replace Elevators 539-24-102
description: Provide complete design services, including all necessary schematics, design development, surveys, cost estimates, construction drawings and specifications, and construction period services (CPS) for solicitation to upgrade and replace all elevators and elevator components at the Cincinnati VA Medical Center, 3200 Vine Street, Cincinnati, OH 45220 and the Ft. Thoms Domiciliary, 1000 S. Ft. Thomas Ave, Ft. Thomas, KY 41075. This project will modernize, replace, and repair 21 elevators that are deteriorated, outdated, or frequently out of service. Several elevators contain obsolete components that are no longer available for purchase, requiring replacement to ensure continued reliability and maintainability. Other units require upgrades to doors, flooring, and ceiling finishes due to normal use and deterioration. SELECTION CRITERIA The Government will evaluate each potential contractor under the terms of its: A. Professional qualifications necessary for satisfactory performance of required services; B. Specialized experience and technical competence in the type of work required, including, where appropriate, experience in energy conservation, pollution prevention, waste reduction, and the use of recovered materials; C. Capacity to accomplish the work in the required time; D. Past performance on contracts with Government agencies and private industry in terms of cost control, quality of work, and compliance with performance schedules; E. Location in the general geographical area of the project and knowledge of the locality of the project; provided, that application of this criterion leaves an appropriate number of qualified firms, given the nature and size of the project; F. Experience in construction period services to include professional field inspections during the construction period, review of construction submittals, support in answering requests for information during the construction period, and support of construction contract changes to include drafting statements of work, and cost estimates shall be included as an evaluation criterion when construction period services is included in the statement of work for A-E services, and; G. The extent to which potential contractors identify and commit to the use of service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses, veteran-owned small businesses, and other types of small businesses as subcontractors. SUBMITTAL INSTRUCTIONS All interested and capable contractors must submit an electronic copy of their SF 330s, via email, by the closing time/date of this announcement. Note the following: No hard/physical copies will be accepted. Limit SF 330 packages to 50 pages. Only the first 50 pages will be evaluated. Submit all documentation as one single file. The total size of the electronic submission (email and all attachments) must not exceed 15MB; larger emails may get rejected by the network server and will be considered non-responsive. Cited relevant projects must be within the last five (5) years. Submit packages via email to the contract specialist by the deadline:� ronald.heidemann@va.gov Subject line must include the notice number: 36C25027R0008 Please include your firm s POC and UEI in the email body. ***End of Presolicitation Notice**

description: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) to obtain a Medicare Administrative Contractor (hereinafter referred to as �the contractor�) to provide specified health insurance benefit administration services, including Medicare claims processing and payment services, in support of the Medicare Program (also known as the Medicare Fee-For-Service or FFS) for Jurisdiction 8. title: Synthetic Signature Generation (SSG) Support Services
description: The Department of the Navy, Naval Surface Warfare Center, Carderock Division (NSWCCD) is soliciting for scientific, engineering, and technical services required for the design, development, fabrication, integration, test, fleet implementation, and maintenance of Synthetic Signature Generation (SSG) based simulation systems. The Government requires support system installations and updates required for the following five categories of Navy fleet training systems: Submarine Team, Navigation, Surface, Surveillance, and On-Board. The Government requires design, development, integration, testing, delivery, installation, and maintenance of fielded systems. The Government requires technical engineering support for simulation and training system capabilities to existing fleet onsite maintenance personnel for the operational systems. The Government also requires support for tactical testing and analysis system configurations for common simulation and tactical subsystems utilized in these trainers. The Government is soliciting this requirement as full-and-open competition. The contract will be awarded as a single award indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity(IDIQ), with Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) Level of Effort (LOE) CLINs and Cost Only Other Direct Costs (ODCs) CLINs for incidental materials and travel. The contract will be for a period of three years to include three one-year ordering periods.

title: Debris Boom Supply and Install at Harry S. Truman Lake Project
description: The solicitation is amended to provide revisions to the Purchase Description, CLIN Structure, provide a Projnet Plan Room key to access the Bathymetry survey information and extend the quote due date. Also, Contractor Questions Answered Part 2 are posted. Contractor Questions/Government Answers are posted. The purpose of the debris boom is to prevent floating debris from impacting the dam's tainter gates, which is crucial for maintaining the full operational capacity of the spillway. The boom will also serve as a visual barrier to boaters. The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, engineering, fabrication, delivery, and optional installation necessary to furnish a complete debris boom system at Harry S. Truman Dam. The approximately 2,000-foot boom shall be designed to intercept floating debris upstream of the spillway and withstand site-specific hydraulic, wind, wave, debris, and impact loading conditions. The debris boom shall be designed for an 800-foot-long by 3-foot-thick debris field, use a minimum safety factor of 2.0 for design loads, withstand a direct head-on impact from an 18-inch-diameter, 100-foot-long log traveling at the maximum design water velocity, and withstand design conditions including 50 mph wind speed and 5-foot wave height. This acquisition is not set-aside for small business concerns and is competed as full and open competition, Unrestricted. An organized site visit has been scheduled for: Friday, 9 October 2026 at 11am.

title: AFLCMC/HNIT seeks expressions of interest regarding a potential commercial coworking space in the environs of Concord, Massachusetts.
description: The purpose of this request for information is to seek responses from interested vendors regarding a potential short-term commercial coworking space service contract for the Enterprise IT as a Service (EITaaS) program, which the agency anticipates that it may award in the summer of 2027. The projected period of performance start date is August 2, 2027. The agency seeks, in particular, responses from vendors that meet the requirements listed below. A draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) has been attached to this notice, which provides additional information on the required services. Responses should clearly indicate whether the vendor believes that it can meet all requirements. If it believes that it cannot, the vendor should specifically identify the requirements that it believes it can meet and those that it believes it cannot meet. Where possible, the vendor shall indicate and describe the particular property or properties that it believes would be suited to this contract, and the nature of its interest in that property (if any). The agency anticipates, in accordance with Department of the Air Force (DAF) Contract Policy Memo 24-C-10, that the PSC shall be X1AB (Lease/Rental of Conference Space and Facilities) and the NAICS shall be 531120. Note that this service contract, if awarded, will be in full accordance with the requirements set forth in the memo. Property Management: The contractor shall provide an environment that meets the requirements outlined in the Performance Work Statement. It shall be approximately within a 6-mile radius of the Concord Town House, 22 Monument Square, Concord, MA (with the approximate coordinates being 42�27'40.1"N 71�20'55.0"W). (The agency may consider an environment outside of this 6-mile radius if it determines that it is in its best interest to do so.) It shall have roughly 30,000 square feet of office space; it shall contain 190 or more workstations, 6 to 8 private �office pods� or �booths� (each of a size sufficient to accommodate one individual), 4 small collaborative spaces (each of a size sufficient to accommodate up to 6 individuals), a commercial lactation pod, and 6 to 8 meeting rooms, with a personnel range of 151-175 individuals when fully operational, and potentially 176-200 individuals to meet future programmatic demands. It shall have a break area/dining area and a shared kitchen area that meet the requirements specified in the PWS. The parking lot or garage shall have a capacity sufficient for all personnel. Within the coworking space, the contractor shall provide a dedicated, private, exclusive fully enclosed office for the operational use of authorized DAF personnel, which meets the security, structural, and other specifications listed in the PWS. IT Support and Maintenance Services: The vendor shall provide IT support for the coworking space�s workstations and conference equipment. It shall provide on-site technical support staffing. It shall monitor the equipment and the IT infrastructure to ensure that equipment is free from defects, that equipment is operable, and that connectivity is maintained. If the vendor observes any actual or potential information security violations in the course of providing this support, it shall report them to the Government Security Manager. Administrative and Janitorial Services: The vendor shall ensure that restrooms are restocked and maintained, that the shared kitchen and kitchen appliances are maintained, that shared kitchen supplies are restocked (including the restocking of the commercial coffee machine and beverage dispenser), that meeting rooms, open seating areas, and other elements of the coworking space are maintained, shall provide front desk staffing, and shall otherwise administer the coworking space in accordance with commercial practices and with agency-specific needs. Software Licenses, Collaboration Licenses, Network Services, Power/Utility Services, and Commercial Wi-Fi: The contractor shall provide these services in accordance with the PWS. Hardware and Enclosures: The contractor shall install and maintain contractor-owned or contractor-leased hardware and equipment (e.g. printers) and shall install and maintain government-owned hardware and equipment (e.g. large-format displays and computer monitors) in accordance with the PWS. It shall permit the installation of a lockable, ventilated, government-owned IT equipment rack or wall-mounted communications cabinet within the dedicated space. This notice is not a solicitation and does not bind the agency in any way. If the agency opts to post a solicitation, it will only consider those bidders that are actively registered on SAM.gov at the time of issuance of the solicitation. Responses are due by 12:00 PM EDT on October 27, 2026, and should be emailed to Contract Specialist Steven C. Bodnar at steven.bodnar@us.af.mil and Contract Specialist Andrew C. St. Maurice at andrew.st_maurice@us.af.mil.

title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE RELATED TO SEVERAL UPCOMING PROJECTS at WRIGHT-PATTERSON AFB, OHIO
description: ***21 October 2026 Update: The responses due date is being revised to 02 Novemeber at 12:00 P.M. Eastern Time. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE RELATED TO SEVERAL UPCOMING PROJECTS at WPAFB, OHIO Notice: This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market research and informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should a formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) 1. PROJECT OVERVIEWS The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), in support of the United States Air Force (USAF), is conducting market research to identify interested and qualified industry partners for the design and construction of several upcoming construction projects at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), Ohio. PROJECT 1: RENOVATE NASIC MAIN CAMPUS, PHASE 1, F/10853 - This project is renovation of 170,000 SF of Sensitive and/or Special Access Program spaces. The work consists of the full renovation of F/10853 through reconfiguration and interior renovation to create a network of administrative functions. The work shall be done in accordance with Intelligence Community Directive 705 (ICD 705) criteria and standards. The interior demolition consists of removal of all architectural and mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) elements including floor, wall, and ceiling finishes. Work includes replacement of building systems, reconfiguration of interior partitions, life safety systems, roof replacement, and envelope modification. The roofing system will be replaced with an energy-compliant system. Penetrations will be added to the building for daylighting, and the exterior envelope will be modified on first floor locations for mechanical rooms. All piping and sprinklers that are part of the current fire protection system are to be replaced. All domestic water, storm, and sanitary piping will be replaced. Additionally, this project includes cybersecurity measures. A corridor bridge connecting F/10828 and F/10856 over an existing loading dock is to be constructed. Personnel will require swing space during the renovation of F/10853. Swing space will be provided through existing available spaces throughout the NASIC IPC campus or via a temporary facility. It is critical that the sequencing of repair work be considered so that available spaces are not overwhelmed. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: Approximately $160,000,000 PROJECT 2: Advanced Materials Research Laboratory � C2A - Construction of an approximately ~90,000 SF three-story laboratory and research facility, as well as the potential construction of a central utility plant for the Air Force Reach Labor Material and Manufacturing Directorate. New facility will consist of concrete, foundation, structural steel frame, masonry etc. Onsite gas boilers for heat and chilled water generation for cooling and lab processes. The interior shall consist of open inter-disciplinary collaboration labs with clean utilities, vibration isolation, precision HVAC and humidity controls, as well as fire protection/suppression, intrusion detections systems and medium voltage switchgear (i.e. 12,470 volts). Site work consists of utilities, sidewalks, parking, communications The new facility shall connect to existing facilities and demolitions of facility 20654. is part of this project. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: Approximately $122,000,000 PROJECT 3: Compressor Research Facility Systems Modernization This project will modernize the Air Force Research Lab�s (AFRL) Compressor Research Facility (CRF) by replacing legacy drive and power equipment with a new 30,000-horsepower Variable Frequency Drive system to support engine component testing. The effort will deliver a fully integrated system that improves reliability, control, maintainability, and long-term test capability. Work includes replacement of the existing drive system with a new 30,000-horsepower VFD with active front end, a new 30,000-horsepower brushless synchronous motor, a new primary transformer, medium-voltage switchgear, protective relaying, and all associated interconnecting cables, bus work, grounding, and terminations. The project also includes the demolition and removal of legacy electrical and mechanical equipment; upgrades to controls, monitoring interfaces, cooling and ventilation systems, and supporting electrical infrastructure; and any required structural, foundation, enclosure, or fire/life-safety modifications needed to install and operate the new equipment. Additional work will include system integration, testing, commissioning, performance verification, operator and maintainer training, and delivery of technical data, recommended spare parts, and warranty support. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $25,000,000 PROJECT 4: Consolidate/Demo F/31240 This project will decentralize Area A heating by replacing the aging high-temperature hot water (HTHW) system fed from Building F/31240, Line A, and Line D with standalone boiler plants serving 49 facilities. The project supports administrative, warehouse, laboratory, hangar, and dormitory buildings that require year-round hot water for heating, reheating, humidity control, and climate management. Work includes facility surveys, evaluation of mechanical room capacity and code compliance, and determination of any needed interior renovations or limited additions to support the new equipment. The project also includes demolition of Building F/31240 and its boiler equipment, removal of above-ground HTHW piping and supports, and capping and abandonment of below-grade piping in place. New high-efficiency boiler systems, pumps, controls, and related accessories will be installed at affected facilities, with evaluation of both natural gas-fired and electric options. Additional work includes mechanical room modifications, make-up water assemblies where needed, upgrades to electrical, fire alarm, fire suppression, and direct digital control systems, and site restoration including pavement repair, grass restoration, and backfill and seeding at the demolished plant site. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $66,500,000 PROJECT 5: Consolidate/Demo West Ramp This project will decentralize heating for the West Ramp area at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base by replacing the existing high-temperature hot water (HTHW) system from Building F/34019 with standalone boiler plants serving 15 surrounding facilities. The effort addresses aging and degraded infrastructure supporting administrative, laboratory, and active hangar facilities that require year-round hot water for comfort heating, reheating, humidity control, and climate management. The project includes surveying each facility to determine boiler locations, evaluating mechanical room walls for code compliance, and assessing whether mechanical room expansions, electrical upgrades, or system improvements are needed to support the new equipment. Work includes demolition and removal of Building F/34019 and its internal boiler equipment, along with demolition of the exterior emergency generator, tank, piping, and all above-ground HTHW piping, supports, and foundations. Below-grade piping will be capped and abandoned in place. Each affected facility will receive new high-efficiency boiler systems, distribution pumps, controls, and related access

title: Systems Engineering Request for Information
description: The Government is conducting market research to identify capable industry partners that can provide systems engineering and integrated logistics support for Navy Enterprise Resource Planning (Navy ERP) Technical Support Services (NETSS) 2, a complex enterprise system supporting more than 70,000 users, across the system lifecycle, including planning, development, integration, testing, deployment, sustainment, and modernization. The anticipated requirement is expected to require a minimum workforce of 15 full-time equivalents (FTEs) with the technical experience necessary to provide coordinated engineering and logistics support for a large, operationally critical enterprise environment. Please find some sample tasks from prior work for context: -Provide technical management and systems engineering support, including engineering assessments, hardware and software integration, interoperability and network analysis, and support to Government engineering teams. -Maintain engineering plans, requirements-management processes, technical baselines, system architectures, and supporting documentation; analyze requirement and design changes; track Requests for Change; maintain traceability through design and testing; and recommend process improvements. -Support SETRs and other technical reviews by assessing readiness, risk, compliance, and technical baselines; preparing reports, briefs, metrics, meeting minutes, and action plans; and tracking actions to closure. -Develop and maintain architecture products, support Model-Based Systems Engineering, evaluate cloud and security considerations, and help implement Agile and DevSecOps practices. -Support testing, releases, and external interfaces by developing test artifacts, analyzing results, coordinating releases and test events, maintaining requirements traceability, and managing Interface Control Agreements and Interface Control Documents. ________________________________________________________________________ This RFI is issued solely for market-research purposes and does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, or commitment by the Government to award a contract. title: AFLCMC/HNIT seeks expressions of interest regarding a potential commercial coworking space in the environs of Concord, Massachusetts.
description: The purpose of this request for information is to seek responses from interested vendors regarding a potential short-term commercial coworking space service contract for the Enterprise IT as a Service (EITaaS) program, which the agency anticipates that it may award in the summer of 2027. The projected period of performance start date is August 2, 2027. The agency seeks, in particular, responses from vendors that meet the requirements listed below. A draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) has been attached to this notice, which provides additional information on the required services. Responses should clearly indicate whether the vendor believes that it can meet all requirements. If it believes that it cannot, the vendor should specifically identify the requirements that it believes it can meet and those that it believes it cannot meet. Where possible, the vendor shall indicate and describe the particular property or properties that it believes would be suited to this contract, and the nature of its interest in that property (if any). The agency anticipates, in accordance with Department of the Air Force (DAF) Contract Policy Memo 24-C-10, that the PSC shall be X1AB (Lease/Rental of Conference Space and Facilities) and the NAICS shall be 531120. Note that this service contract, if awarded, will be in full accordance with the requirements set forth in the memo. Property Management: The contractor shall provide an environment that meets the requirements outlined in the Performance Work Statement. It shall be approximately within a 6-mile radius of the Concord Town House, 22 Monument Square, Concord, MA (with the approximate coordinates being 42�27'40.1"N 71�20'55.0"W). (The agency may consider an environment outside of this 6-mile radius if it determines that it is in its best interest to do so.) It shall have roughly 30,000 square feet of office space; it shall contain 190 or more workstations, 6 to 8 private �office pods� or �booths� (each of a size sufficient to accommodate one individual), 4 small collaborative spaces (each of a size sufficient to accommodate up to 6 individuals), a commercial lactation pod, and 6 to 8 meeting rooms, with a personnel range of 151-175 individuals when fully operational, and potentially 176-200 individuals to meet future programmatic demands. It shall have a break area/dining area and a shared kitchen area that meet the requirements specified in the PWS. The parking lot or garage shall have a capacity sufficient for all personnel. Within the coworking space, the contractor shall provide a dedicated, private, exclusive fully enclosed office for the operational use of authorized DAF personnel, which meets the security, structural, and other specifications listed in the PWS. It shall monitor the equipment and the IT infrastructure to ensure that equipment is free from defects, that equipment is operable, and that connectivity is maintained. If the vendor observes any actual or potential information security violations in the course of providing this support, it shall report them to the Government Security Manager. Administrative and Janitorial Services: The vendor shall ensure that restrooms are restocked and maintained, that the shared kitchen and kitchen appliances are maintained, that shared kitchen supplies are restocked (including the restocking of the commercial coffee machine and beverage dispenser), that meeting rooms, open seating areas, and other elements of the coworking space are maintained, shall provide front desk staffing, and shall otherwise administer the coworking space in accordance with commercial practices and with agency-specific needs. It shall permit the installation of a lockable, ventilated, government-owned IT equipment rack or wall-mounted communications cabinet within the dedicated space. PROJECT OVERVIEWS The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), in support of the United States Air Force (USAF), is conducting market research to identify interested and qualified industry partners for the design and construction of several upcoming construction projects at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), Ohio. PROJECT 1: RENOVATE NASIC MAIN CAMPUS, PHASE 1, F/10853 - This project is renovation of 170,000 SF of Sensitive and/or Special Access Program spaces. The work consists of the full renovation of F/10853 through reconfiguration and interior renovation to create a network of administrative functions. The work shall be done in accordance with Intelligence Community Directive 705 (ICD 705) criteria and standards. The interior demolition consists of removal of all architectural and mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) elements including floor, wall, and ceiling finishes. Work includes replacement of building systems, reconfiguration of interior partitions, life safety systems, roof replacement, and envelope modification. The roofing system will be replaced with an energy-compliant system. Penetrations will be added to the building for daylighting, and the exterior envelope will be modified on first floor locations for mechanical rooms. All piping and sprinklers that are part of the current fire protection system are to be replaced. All domestic water, storm, and sanitary piping will be replaced. Additionally, this project includes cybersecurity measures. A corridor bridge connecting F/10828 and F/10856 over an existing loading dock is to be constructed. Personnel will require swing space during the renovation of F/10853. Swing space will be provided through existing available spaces throughout the NASIC IPC campus or via a temporary facility. It is critical that the sequencing of repair work be considered so that available spaces are not overwhelmed. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: Approximately $160,000,000 PROJECT 2: Advanced Materials Research Laboratory � C2A - Construction of an approximately ~90,000 SF three-story laboratory and research facility, as well as the potential construction of a central utility plant for the Air Force Reach Labor Material and Manufacturing Directorate. New facility will consist of concrete, foundation, structural steel frame, masonry etc. Onsite gas boilers for heat and chilled water generation for cooling and lab processes. The interior shall consist of open inter-disciplinary collaboration labs with clean utilities, vibration isolation, precision HVAC and humidity controls, as well as fire protection/suppression, intrusion detections systems and medium voltage switchgear (i.e. 12,470 volts). Site work consists of utilities, sidewalks, parking, communications The new facility shall connect to existing facilities and demolitions of facility 20654. is part of this project. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: Approximately $122,000,000 PROJECT 3: Compressor Research Facility Systems Modernization This project will modernize the Air Force Research Lab�s (AFRL) Compressor Research Facility (CRF) by replacing legacy drive and power equipment with a new 30,000-horsepower Variable Frequency Drive system to support engine component testing. The effort will deliver a fully integrated system that improves reliability, control, maintainability, and long-term test capability. Work includes replacement of the existing drive system with a new 30,000-horsepower VFD with active front end, a new 30,000-horsepower brushless synchronous motor, a new primary transformer, medium-voltage switchgear, protective relaying, and all associated interconnecting cables, bus work, grounding, and terminations. The project also includes the demolition and removal of legacy electrical and mechanical equipment; upgrades to controls, monitoring interfaces, cooling and ventilation systems, and supporting electrical infrastructure; and any required structural, foundation, enclosure, or fire/life-safety modifications needed to install and operate the new equipment. Additional work will include system integration, testing, commissioning, performance verification, operator and maintainer training, and delivery of technical data, recommended spare parts, and warranty support. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $25,000,000 PROJECT 4: Consolidate/Demo F/31240 This project will decentralize Area A heating by replacing the aging high-temperature hot water (HTHW) system fed from Building F/31240, Line A, and Line D with standalone boiler plants serving 49 facilities. The project supports administrative, warehouse, laboratory, hangar, and dormitory buildings that require year-round hot water for heating, reheating, humidity control, and climate management. Work includes facility surveys, evaluation of mechanical room capacity and code compliance, and determination of any needed interior renovations or limited additions to support the new equipment. The project also includes demolition of Building F/31240 and its boiler equipment, removal of above-ground HTHW piping and supports, and capping and abandonment of below-grade piping in place. New high-efficiency boiler systems, pumps, controls, and related accessories will be installed at affected facilities, with evaluation of both natural gas-fired and electric options. Additional work includes mechanical room modifications, make-up water assemblies where needed, upgrades to electrical, fire alarm, fire suppression, and direct digital control systems, and site restoration including pavement repair, grass restoration, and backfill and seeding at the demolished plant site. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $66,500,000 PROJECT 5: Consolidate/Demo West Ramp This project will decentralize heating for the West Ramp area at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base by replacing the existing high-temperature hot water (HTHW) system from Building F/34019 with standalone boiler plants serving 15 surrounding facilities. The effort addresses aging and degraded infrastructure supporting administrative, laboratory, and active hangar facilities that require year-round hot water for comfort heating, reheating, humidity control, and climate management. The project includes surveying each facility to determine boiler locations, evaluating mechanical room walls for code compliance, and assessing whether mechanical room expansions, electrical upgrades, or system improvements are needed to support the new equipment. Work includes demolition and removal of Building F/34019 and its internal boiler equipment, along with demolition of the exterior emergency generator, tank, piping, and all above-ground HTHW piping, supports, and foundations. Below-grade piping will be capped and abandoned in place. Each affected facility will receive new high-efficiency boiler systems, distribution pumps, controls, and related access

description: Network Contracting Office (NCO) - VA South Texas (VASTHCS) facilities intends to award a sole source contract for all labor, equipment, supervision and expertise, to provide maintenance services bed rental equipment to the VA North Texas Health Care System (VANTXHCS), 4500 South Lancaster Road, Dallas, Texas 75216, for the sole purpose of patient care for our residents and are within defined time frames for services. The purpose of this action is to establish a lease contract for Rotoprone E beds. The Dallas VA Health Care Center provides standard hospital beds for all hospitalized patients; however, in certain circumstances such as specific respiratory or medical conditions the mattress and/or the entire bed frame must be replaced to ensure optimal patient care. These specialized surfaces are obtained through short term leases for the duration of treatment. The Rotoprone Therapy System bed is the only automated system that allows caregivers to deliver multiple intervals of prone therapy over an extended period. The Rotoprone Therapy System helps manage patient handling risks associated with manual proning, improves oxygenation, protects against ventilator induced lung injury, and reduces mortality. title: Sole Source to Rosemount Inc for annual maintenance, calibration, linearization, and recertification of up to (10) Emerson model MLT analyzers and up to (14) Xstream model analyzers
description: This procurement is a Sole Source to Rosemount Inc for annual maintenance, calibration, linearization, and recertification of up to (10) Emerson model MLT analyzers and up to (14) Xstream model analyzers per the attached justification. The Navy Experimental Diving Unit (NEDU) currently has a requirement for annual maintenance, calibration, linearization, and recertification of up to (10) Emerson model MLT analyzers and up to (14) Xstream model analyzers at NEDU. As the manufacturer of the instrument, ROSEMOUNT, Inc. (subsidiary: EMERSON LLLP) is the only company offering service and recertification of the equipment. To use another company to conduct recertification on this equipment might compromise their overall performance. Use of another vendor may change or introduce new parameters that may be harmful to all diving systems tested and maintained at NEDU, and negatively affect the diving and life support systems these instruments are vital components of. Therefore, it is imperative that this particular vendor be used to limit the risk to life and health of the US Navy Divers who depend on this instrument. Therefore, it is in the Government�s best interest to award on a sole source basis to ROSEMOUNT, Inc. See attached justification.

title: 6515--Inventory Management System
description: THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. SUBMISSION OF INFORMATION ABOUT PRICING, DELIVERY, THE MARKET, AND CAPABILITIES IS HIGHLY ENCOURAGED AND ALLOWED UNDER THIS RFI FOR PLANNING PURPOSES IN ACCORDANCE WITH (IAW) FAR 15.201(e). DISCLAIMER This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly. IAW FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. SOURCES SOUGHT/RFI DESCRIPTION This is NOT a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice / RFI only. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice / RFI is to gain information about potential qualified sources and their size classification relative to NAICS code is 334519 - Other Measuring and Controlling Device Manufacturing, with an SBA small business size standard of 600 employees. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice / RFI will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. After review of the responses to this Sources Sought Notice / RFI, further RFIs and/or a solicitation or other announcements may be published. The purpose of this procurement is to acquire and install a fully automated, weight-based inventory management system, brand name or equal to PAR Excellence, for the VA Phoenix Healthcare System. The system is intended to provide accurate, real-time perpetual inventory visibility while minimizing end-user data entry and supporting timely replenishment of medical and surgical supplies. The anticipated requirement includes all equipment, scales, controllers, storage products, mounting hardware and accessories, software licenses, interfaces, implementation services, installation, configuration, testing, training, warranty, monitoring, maintenance, and technical support necessary to deliver a fully operational system at the facility's designated primary and secondary supply locations. For market-research and planning purposes, the anticipated configuration is approximately 26 PAR Bins Replenish software licenses, 3,571 scales of various types and capacities, 27 Ethernet replenishment controllers, related hardware accessories, storage bins, shelving, cabinets, mobile louvered panel units, and associated implementation and training services. Final quantities and configurations are subject to change. At a minimum, the proposed solution must provide an HL7 interface that communicates with the VA Generic Inventory Package (GIP) in VistA and must have an approved VA Information Technology Authority to Operate (ATO) at the time of offer. Contractors must be able to validate interoperability with VA GIP through the HL7 interface prior to award. The system must support unlimited users and multiple permission levels; provide access from multiple points on VA-furnished computers; produce Excel or text-delimited reports; display equipment and materials-management status; provide item-location, PAR-level analysis, consumption data, order, reconciliation, due-in/due-out, discrepancy, and inventory-value reporting; and generate pick-ticket information based on PAR levels, reorder points, and emergency stock levels. The system must be compatible with existing shelving, cabinets, carts, and other storage infrastructure; accommodate medical and surgical products of varying size, thickness, and weight, including products up to approximately 3 feet long by 2 feet wide and 20 pounds; and permit VA employees to recalibrate the system for different package quantities. The contractor must install and configure the required software on VA-furnished equipment, provide staff training, furnish a one-year license agreement with software upgrades, and provide 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, 365 days per year support. Support must include at least four remote equipment-functionality checks every 24 hours, response to service calls within 24 hours, and repair or replacement of covered equipment or hardware within 48 hours when damage or defect is not attributable to VA personnel. Installation is anticipated to begin no later than 70 days after contract award and be completed no later than 400 days after award, subject to facility deployment planning and required facility tasks. Deliverables will be shipped to VA Phoenix Healthcare System, Main Warehouse (ATTN: Prentiss Logan), 650 E Indian School Road, Phoenix, AZ 85012, with notice to the Contracting Officer's Representative five business days before shipment. The current independent planning estimate derived from the attached vendor quotation is $1,502,945.49, inclusive of turnkey installation. This amount is provided solely to describe the anticipated magnitude of the requirement for market-research purposes and does not constitute a Government estimate, commitment, or solicitation price. STATEMENT OF WORK 1. Background VA Phoenix Healthcare System has used cabinet-based Point of Use (POU) systems to manage inventory levels within our facility s supply areas. Our facility s current supply system process relies heavily on clinical staff entering quantities as they pull product. When they fail to enter, or enter incorrect quantities, our process fails. This leads to workload issues, as Supply Techs must be pulled from current duties to perform urgent resupply requests to affected areas. This also presents potential patient safety issues during emergency situations if stock is not available due to inaccurate stock level information. Further, the current supply process is labor and time intensive. This is compounded in times of heavy workload due to availability of supply personnel and/or hospital patient load, increasing risks associated with patient care / safety. VA Phoenix Healthcare System is looking for a fully automated weight-based inventory management system that does not require end users to input data or interface with the system to increase or decrease material items stocked or consumed by the user. The station requires a system that removes or heavily limits the amount of human interface required to maintain accurate and real time inventories. This creates a more accurate and efficient system while simultaneously addressing the patient safety / care concerns mentioned above, eliminating the frequent emergent supply requests created by inadequate inventory management systems. A fully automated weight-based inventory management system will augment the supply chain s management effectiveness and timeliness with resupply inventory while decreasing the workload of supply personnel. It will also improve the overall patient care throughout the facility, particularly in the cardiac catheterization and electrophysiology labs, by effectively maintaining appropriate periodic automatic replacement levels. 2. Scope The scope of this requirement is to obtain and install an automated inventory management system at VA Phoenix Healthcare System, ensure system is fully operational, and fully train staff to be knowledgeable on the use of system. This is a brand name or equal requirement; a Fully Automated Weight-Based Inventory Management System or equal to PAR Excellence. Contractors must provide a brand name or equal that meets or exceeds the physical, functional, and performance of listed characteristics described in this Statement of Work. Contractor must show clear and compelling, and convincing evidence that all equal to items meet all required salient characteristics including brand name and model numbers IAW FAR 52.211-6 Brand Name or Equal. title: KC-135 Center Console Refresh (CCR) Revision 2
description: 01 Oct 26 Amendment 05 was issued to revised paragraphs 13.5 and 13.14 of the SOW, Add Clause H005 and remove RFO clause 52.246-17 from the solicitation. Due to these changes, the proposal due date is extended to 09 Nov 26 at 12:00pm CDT. 17 Sept 26 The conformed contract, incorporating Amendments 01 through 04, is now available. 03 Sep 26 Amendment 04 was issued with minor corrections to Attachment 1 Statement of Work and Attachments 3a/3b to correct some links in the pricing matrixes. The proposal due date remains 02 Nov 26. 31 Aug 26 Amendment 03 issued with a revised Attachment 2 SRD, Attachment 3a Pricing Matrix, and removal of Clause H005. Solicitation Due date changed to 02 Nov 26 at 12:00pm CST. 24 Aug 26 Editable PDF versions of the previously released Solicitation and Amendments are available. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged and in full force and effect. Reminder, the Solicitation and Amendments must be signed and included with the proposal submission. 12 August Amendment 02 to revise documents as a result of Q&A. 28 Jul 26 Amendment 01 to revised documents as a result of Q&A. 10 Jul 26 Center Console Refresh addresses critical obsolescence issues within the KC-135 Refueling Tanker aircraft. The US Air Force needs an updated Fuel System (FS), Flight Display System (FDS), and Flight Computer due to obsolescence and is looking for innovative ideas to not only replace but improve these systems with turn-key solutions enabling supportability and future growth. The FS, FDS, Flight Computer, and the future growth/adaptability define the scope of the CCR program. The program scope also includes the addition of autothrottle systems. The anticipated contract will be a Cost-Plus Incentive Fee (CPIF) for EMD, Firm Fixed Price (FFP) for Production and Deployment (P&D), single award indefinite delivery/quantity type contract comprised of One (1) 48-month Base Period with Six (6) 1-Year Option Periods and a projected period of performance from July 2028 to June 2038.
